input: Read /doc/README.md and generate a table of contents from its headings (lines starting with # or ##). Insert the TOC after the first heading, formatted as a markdown list with '- [Heading Text](#anchor)' where anchor is the heading text lowercased with spaces replaced by hyphens. Write the result back to the file.

transcript.final_response:
Done. `/doc/README.md` now has a table of contents inserted right after the first heading (`# Project Alpha`), formatted as a markdown list linking to lowercase, hyphenated anchors:

- [Project Alpha](#project-alpha)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [API Reference](#api-reference)
- [Contributing](#contributing)

The rest of the document content is preserved unchanged.
tool_calls:
cd /doc && {
  line=$(head -1 README.md)
  rest=$(tail -n +2 README.md)
  printf '%s\n\n' "$line" > README.md.new
  # build TOC from headings
  printf '%s\n%s\n' "$line" "$rest" | grep -E '^#{1,2} ' | while IFS= read -r h; do
    text=${h#*# }
    anchor=$(printf '%s' "$text" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr ' ' '-')
    printf -- '- [%s](#%s)\n' "$text" "$anchor"
  done >> README.md.new
  printf '\n%s\n' "$rest" >> README.md.new
  mv README.md.new README.md
}
cat /doc/README.md
cd /doc && awk 'BEGIN{p=0} /^$/{if(p)next;p=1;print;next} {p=0;print}' README.md > README.md.tmp && mv README.md.tmp README.md && cat README.md
